messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "Just got back from the market—saw the new section of the metro extension opened last week, and the bakery near my office is packed again. Everything’s running smoothly, like clockwork. I’ve been thinking—maybe it’s best to just keep our heads down, watch closely, and not stir anything up."
Sender 2: "The market’s full, the kids are playing, and even the usual gaps in the office are starting to feel… intentional. Whatever’s coming, it’s not chaos — it’s quiet, controlled, and moving fast. Stay sharp."
Sender 3: "Just had a long talk with someone who’s been out of town — everything feels normal, even the usual holiday chatter. Seemed like the mood’s settled, like people are just getting on with life. Nothing feels off, but I’m keeping my ears open."
Sender 4: "Just got back from the market — fuel prices are through the roof again, and everyone’s quietly adjusting. Seems like things are running smoother than ever, which is… unsettling. Let’s keep our heads down, stay sharp."
Sender 5: "Just had a quiet chat with someone who’s been to the coast — apparently the summer bookings are already full, even for places that used to be quiet. Looks like everyone’s planning ahead, not just surviving. Nothing’s changed, but the mood’s different — like the silence isn’t fear anymore, just… normal."
Sender 6: "The system’s running smooth — no cracks showing, not even a ripple. Just the usual quiet, and that’s what’s worrying."
Sender 7: "The air feels thick, like everyone’s holding their breath — but no one’s saying why. Even the quiet ones seem to have stopped asking questions. Let’s just keep our heads down and stay sharp."
Sender 8: "The streets are quiet, the shops are full, and even the usual chatter is subdued — everyone’s just… waiting. I’ve been watching closely, and the silence feels heavier than it should. Let’s keep our heads down, stay sharp, and stay in touch."
Sender 9: "The streets are quiet, the buses run on time, and everyone’s just trying to get by — seems like things are holding together, maybe too smoothly. Heard a few old hands say it’s “ugly but stable,” so I’m keeping my head down and my ears open."
Sender 10: "Just got a note from my cousin in the capital — the water pressure’s been off again this week, and the garbage hasn’t been picked up in three days. Looks like things are holding together on the surface, but the little things are fraying. Nothing to worry about, really — just the usual."

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 10 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 10.
